interpreted_intent: One unmistakably adult fashion subject continues an unfinished self-directed fastening action that visibly changes or holds one exact stable garment boundary. That boundary reveals or re-covers one bounded non-explicit collarbone, shoulder, side, back, or clearly distinct opaque foundation-layer relation. Face, action, torso, readable private-room context, material overlap, contact shadow, and gravity remain legible together. Face and the changed boundary are the first two readable focal relations after thumbnail reduction, and closing or removing that boundary erases the controlled-reveal proposition.
subject: one unmistakably adult woman with visible adult facial proportions, long dark wavy hair, and visible natural skin texture; the supplied reference is limited to those appearance cues
setting: an adult apartment bedroom beside a linen-curtained window during a snow-bright late afternoon, with a folded linen scarf on one chair
event: her right thumb and forefinger physically pinch the upper wrap edge and its small fabric loop at the same left-collarbone boundary, holding the unfinished fastening midway so the bounded cream opaque foundation layer remains visible
visual_priorities: the visible hand-to-fastener-to-garment-boundary causal chain reads immediately
the adult face and changed collarbone boundary are the first two readable focal relations at thumbnail scale
private-room context, fabric overlap, contact shadow, and gravity stay legible in one frame
baseline_prompt_en: Create a photorealistic, non-explicit adult fashion-editorial photograph in an adult apartment bedroom beside a linen-curtained window during a snow-bright late afternoon. Show one unmistakably adult woman with long dark wavy hair, visible adult facial proportions, and visible natural skin texture. Frame her from mid-torso upward as she stands near the window in a moss-green brushed-cotton wrap blouse over a cream opaque foundation top. Her right thumb and forefinger physically pinch the upper wrap edge and its small fabric loop at the same left-collarbone boundary, holding the unfinished fastening midway. That hand visibly draws the moss-green edge inward while a bounded triangle of collarbone and the cream opaque foundation layer remains visible between the overlapping fabric edges. The finger pressure, pulled fabric tension, narrow contact shadow, doubled edge thickness, and downward drape make cause and gravity unmistakable. Keep her calm adult face and the changed collarbone boundary as the first two readable focal relations, with her hand fully visible between them. A folded linen scarf rests on one chair, supporting an ordinary private-room moment without competing for attention. Use snow-reflected window light to shape her face and the material overlap together, preserving pores, small flyaway hairs, brushed-cotton nap, and realistic cloth weight. The supplied reference guides only visible adult facial proportions, long dark wavy hair, and natural skin texture.
